__ferrum_note: Every PromQL expression below names only metric families the shipped binaries actually export, and metrics_gate.rs::every_metric_this_dashboard_charts_is_one_the_binaries_export fails the build if that stops being true. The reverse direction is held too: a family exported and charted nowhere must be named in NOT_CHARTED with a reason.
title: FERRUM — enforcement plane

panels.title: Nodes not attached to the kernel
panels.description: ferrum_agent_degraded_reason{reason="not_attached"} is 1 on a node where nothing feeds the decision path. Such a node reports Ready and enforces nothing. Anything but 0 here is the alert.

panels.title: Degraded nodes
panels.description: ferrum_agent_degraded is the whole degraded state as one bool; the breakdown below says which reason.

panels.title: Bundle digests in force (agents)
panels.description: One value while a rollout is settled; two or more means the fleet is split across bundles. Digest and not policy name on purpose: a content hash names no policy.

panels.title: Bundle digests in force (webhook)
panels.description: Replicas of the webhook disagreeing about the bundle is a rollout that has not converged; under failurePolicy: Fail that means two different verdicts for the same Pod depending on which replica answers.

panels.title: Degradation reasons across the fleet
panels.description: Every reason this build can raise is published on every scrape, 0 included, so a flat line at zero means 'not raised' and a gap means 'not scraped'. The two are different and this panel can tell them apart.

panels.title: In-kernel ring drops per second
panels.description: ferrum_agent_events_dropped_total is the in-kernel counter: records the ring dropped under flood, which no rule ever saw. Enforcement missed, on a node that otherwise reports healthy. This is the counter that existed inside the process for eight cycles with no reader.

panels.title: Records that failed to decode
panels.description: The other side of the ring: a record that arrived and no rule could read. Same loss, different half.

panels.title: Enforcement events lost on export
panels.description: A kill that happened and was not written down is the repudiation case. Three separate losses, kept separate: a full queue, a failed write, and a writer that is gone for good.

targets.legendFormat: lost, as the agent counts it

panels.title: Identity the datapath could not resolve
Selectors resolved against a cold cache
panels.description: labels_unknown and identity_unknown are fail-closed resolutions, not non-matches: the rules were applied without the facts they select on.

panels.title: Container map
panels.description: Until the cgroups the index knows are in the kernel map, EVENT_FLAG_CONTAINER is never set and every containerOnly rule misses.

panels.title: Paths the kernel could not carry whole
panels.description: A truncated path is a suffix rule decided without the bytes it names. The rule still fired — on an assertion.

panels.title: Signals sent and refused
panels.description: A refusal is a guard doing its job; a failure is a kill the agent tried and could not deliver, and a stale target is one it refused because the tgid may have been reused. The three are not one number.

panels.title: Waivers held on the nodes
panels.description: A waiver that joins nothing is signed, verified, in scope, and demotes nothing here. A table that was dropped enforces stricter than the policy that was signed.

panels.title: Review latency inside the process
panels.description: p50/p90/p99 of the span the API server is blocked on in this process. The socket and the TLS handshake are outside it deliberately: a budget stated on a number that includes the network is one nobody can act on. The red step is the declared budget, 5 ms — the same number ferrum_admission::REVIEW_LATENCY_BUDGET_SECONDS holds and latency_gate.rs measures against; a panel whose threshold disagreed with the code would draw a line nobody could act on either.

panels.title: Verdicts per second
panels.description: A deny wave with no policy change behind it is usually the bundle or the waiver table, not the policy — see the panel to the right.

panels.title: What the webhook lost hold of
panels.description: A poll loop that stopped seeing changes, a bundle key that vanished from the mount, and a waiver table emptied by either. Each of these makes the webhook enforce something other than what was published, without the policy having changed.

panels.title: Waivers the webhook would apply
panels.description: Compare with the node-side count: the two planes read one signed table, and a disagreement between them is a rollout in flight or a Secret only one of them can read.

panels.title: Is the reporting surface itself down
panels.description: status.json unwritable, the clock floor unpersisted, the bundle mount unreadable, and — the meta one — status.json keys this build could not turn into a metric. Anything but zero on the last means a counter exists on the node that this dashboard cannot see.

targets.legendFormat: nodes whose status file will not write
nodes with an in-memory-only rollback floor
nodes whose bundle mount will not stat
failed writes of the rollback floor
failed stats of the bundle mount
controller whose status file will not write

panels.title: Is admission enforcement suspended, and can it be
panels.description: While `suspended` is above zero the webhook answers allow to every AdmissionReview without evaluating anything, and `admitted without evaluation` counts the objects that went in that way. `armed` is the one to read on a quiet day: zero means no replica can break glass at all, so the emergency lever is absent rather than unused. `refused` moving while `suspended` is zero is a grant being rejected on every poll — a wrong key, a stale window, or somebody trying. `journal stopped` above zero is a replica that can no longer record a suspension, and while it is set no grant comes into force.

targets.legendFormat: seconds left on the grant in force
replicas whose journal stopped accepting entries

panels.title: Prevented, or only detected
panels.description: Which half of the loaded policy this fleet stops before it happens. Rules the in-kernel hook cannot decide stay on the tracepoint path and are excluded — a rule naming a path is excluded by construction, the toolchain cannot read one, and the §D acceptance rule «exec + /bin/sh -> kill» is among them — so a non-zero excluded count is the ordinary state and not a fault. `refused` counts nodes whose whole policy may not be enforced in kernel (a non-enforce mode, a disabled policy); `unsynced` is the one that is a fault: the map was cleared, so those nodes prevent nothing and keep detecting.

targets.legendFormat: nodes with the LSM hook attached
nodes whose policy the kernel may not enforce
nodes whose rule set failed to publish
pods the policy selects (0 under an unselected policy)

panels.title: Bundle digests the controller has signed
panels.description: One digest is a converged rollout. Two means the controller signed something the fleet has not taken up yet — compare with the two digest counts at the top of this dashboard: controller, webhook and agents disagreeing is a rollout that did not land, and it is invisible from any one of the three alone.

panels.title: Controller degraded
panels.description: The whole degraded state as one bool, the same one status.json reports. Which class and why is the panel to the right; the cause text stays in the file on the Pod, which is deliberate — a reason is prose and would be an unbounded label.

panels.title: Is the control plane converging
panels.description: Reconciles taken up against the ways they end. A policy that did not compile is the policy author's and the object carries the reason in its own status; the four failure classes are requests to the API server that did not answer, and those are the operator's. Two lines and not one sum, because they send different people.

panels.title: Where the controller is stuck
panels.description: A run climbing towards ferrum_controller_terminal_run in a class that has never succeeded is the deployment being wrong — a mis-edited RBAC, a CRD never applied — and the process ends itself when it arrives, which is why the threshold is charted beside the run instead of restated in an alert. Unactionable objects are the other kind: work that stays undone until a human edits something, and no retry will mend it.
